```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod_name <- "Eigenmann_2017_erlotinib_gefitinib_mouse"
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(mod_name))
# Typical-value model: between-animal variability and residual error removed.
tv <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::zeroRe(ui))
# kel and vc must not trigger rxode2's automatic linear-compartment solve.
stopifnot(is.null(ui$linCmt))
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-017-9553-x>
* Supplement: Supplementary material 1 (DOCX), with the study design (Table
  S1), the missing-data summary (Table S2), the Berkeley Madonna code of the
  three simulation studies (S3, S4, S5) and the random-effect correlation
  matrix (Table S7).

Crossref lists no correction or erratum for this article (checked 2026-11-25).

Eigenmann 2017 fitted two semi-mechanistic tumor growth inhibition (TGI)
models jointly to erlotinib- and gefitinib-treated patient-derived NSCLC
xenograft mice: a base TGI model (Equations 4-8) and an acquired resistance
model (Equations 9-14), which had the lower AIC and residual error (Table 1).
Only the acquired resistance model has published parameter estimates
(Table 2), so it is the model distributed here.

# Population

Patient-derived NSCLC (LXFA677) xenograft mice were randomised into seven
groups of 8 (56 animals): vehicle, and erlotinib or gefitinib at 6.25, 25 or
100 mg/kg given orally once daily on days 3-16. The erlotinib 100 mg/kg group
had a drug holiday for dose-limiting toxicity and was dosed on days 3-10 and
14-16 (Supplementary Table S1). Tumor volume was measured by caliper every
2-3 days over 30 days, and sparse PK samples were taken on days 10 and 16.
Seven percent of the tumor observations were missing (Supplementary Table S2),
and values below the limit of quantification were treated as missing. The
PK model and its individual estimates come from the authors' earlier report
on the same study (Eigenmann 2016, Mol Cancer Ther 15:3110) and were held
fixed while the PD parameters were estimated in Monolix 4.2.2.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb(mod_name)()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source; the table
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| PK: `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)`, `Cc = central / (V - D * I)` | - | Equations 1-3; supplement S3 code |
| `lka` | log(55) 1/day, fixed | Table 2 (X) |
| `lkel`, `lkel_gefitinib` | log(7.56), log(3.87) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lvc`, `lvc_gefitinib` | log(0.127), log(1.40) L | Table 2 |
| `e_cohdose_vc` (I) | 0.00772 L per mg/kg (gefitinib; 0 for erlotinib) | Table 2, Equation 3, Methods 'Covariates' |
| Sensitive cells `d/dt(cycling_cells)` | - | Equation 10 |
| Damaged cells `d/dt(damaged_cells1..3)` | - | Equations 11-13 |
| Resistant cells `d/dt(resistant_cells)` | - | Equations 14, 15, 17; supplement S5 code |
| `tumor_vol = S + T1 + T2 + T3 + R` | - | Equation 9 |
| `ltumorExpGrowth` (lambda0) | log(0.217) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `ltumorLinGrowth` (lambda1) | log(42.8) mm^3/day | Table 2 |
| `lgrowthRatio_resistant` (beta) | log(0.869) | Table 2 |
| `ldamageTransit` (k1) | log(1.52) 1/day | Table 2; tau = 3 / k1 = 1.97 day (Equation 16) |
| `lkmut`, `lkmut_highdose` (kSR) | log(7.4e-3), log(1.7e-3) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `ldrugSlope`, `ldrugSlope_highdose` (k2 erlotinib) | log(9.21e-5), log(3.15e-4) L/ug/day | Table 2 |
| `ldrugSlope_gefitinib` (k2 gefitinib) | log(6.19e-4) L/ug/day | Table 2 |
| `drugSlope_resistant` (k2R) | 0, fixed | Fig. 1 legend; simulations use 9.21e-5 (S4, S5 code) |
| `lcthres` (Cth) | log(7152) ug/L, fixed | Equation 18; S4, S5 code |
| IIV variances | Table 2 'Random effect' squared | Table 2 |
| `propSd_tumor_vol` | 0.136 | Table 1 |
| `addSd_tumor_vol`, `propSd` | 0, fixed (not reported) | Methods 'Parameter estimation' |
| `TUM_VOL` (initial sensitive-cell volume) | covariate; 107 mm^3 in the authors' code | Equation 10; S3-S5 code |

## Units

Time is in days. Doses are amounts in ug for a 25 g mouse: the authors' code
converts mg/kg to ug with `C = 25`, so 100 mg/kg is 2500 ug. With V in L the
plasma concentration `Cc` is in ug/L and k2 in L/ug/day, as in Table 2. The
dose group itself, in mg/kg, is the `COHDOSE` covariate that enters the
gefitinib volume.

## Covariates

```{r covariates}
str(ui$allCovs)
```

* `TRT_GEFITINIB`: 1 for gefitinib, 0 for erlotinib.
* `DOSE_HIGH`: 1 for the 100 mg/kg group.
* `COHDOSE`: dose group in mg/kg.
* `TUM_VOL`: tumor volume at the start of the study, in mm^3.

```{r helpers}
# Event table for one or more animals. `doses` has columns id, time, amt (ug);
# covariates are given per id in `covs`.
make_events <- function(doses, covs, obs_times) {
  dose_rows <- doses |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = covs$id, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    left_join(covs, by = "id") |>
    as.data.frame()
}

one_animal <- function(drug = c("erlotinib", "gefitinib"), mgkg, tum_vol = 107) {
  drug <- match.arg(drug)
  data.frame(
    id = 1L,
    TRT_GEFITINIB = as.integer(drug == "gefitinib"),
    DOSE_HIGH = as.integer(mgkg >= 100),
    COHDOSE = mgkg,
    TUM_VOL = tum_vol
  )
}

# Trapezoidal area under a tumor-volume curve (the paper's AUCE).
auc_trap <- function(time, y) {
  sum(diff(time) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
}

value_at <- function(sim, t, col) sim[[col]][which.min(abs(sim$time - t))]
```

# Typical-value PK and PKNCA check

The paper reports no NCA, so PKNCA is checked against the closed form of the
one-compartment oral model, `AUC(0-inf) = Dose / (ke * V)`, for one
100 mg/kg dose of each drug.

```{r pk-single}
obs_pk <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0.001, 0.05, by = 0.001), seq(0.05, 3, by = 0.01))))
pk_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(c("erlotinib", "gefitinib"), function(drug) {
  ev <- make_events(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 100 * 25),
    one_animal(drug, 100),
    obs_pk
  )
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(tv, ev)) |>
    mutate(id = 1L, treatment = drug)
}))

conc <- pk_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 2500,
  treatment = c("erlotinib", "gefitinib")
)
pk_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
pk_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
pk_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  pk_conc, pk_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
    aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
)
nca <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(pk_data)$result)

expected <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("erlotinib", "gefitinib"),
  auc_expected = c(
    2500 / (7.56 * 0.127),
    2500 / (3.87 * (1.40 - 0.00772 * 100))
  )
)
nca_wide <- nca |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(expected, by = "treatment")
nca_wide |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug" = treatment, "Cmax (ug/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (day)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (ug*day/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (day)" = half.life,
    "Dose / (ke * V)" = auc_expected
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# Same drawn parameters on both sides, so a tight bound is correct here.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs / nca_wide$auc_expected - 1) < 0.01),
  abs(nca_wide$half.life[nca_wide$treatment == "erlotinib"] - log(2) / 7.56) < 0.005
)
```

The erlotinib Cmax after 100 mg/kg, about 14,300 ug/L, matches the peaks of
the PK trace in Figure 5. At 100 mg/kg the gefitinib volume falls from 1.40 L
to 1.40 - 0.772 = 0.628 L (Equation 3).

# Figure 5: two treatment cycles of erlotinib 100 mg/kg

Figure 5 simulates 100 mg/kg erlotinib on days 3-8 and 14-16. The
authors' code S3 uses the high-dose potency k2 but the low/mid-dose
conversion rate kSR = 0.0074 1/day, and Figure 5 is reproduced only with that
combination, so the simulation below sets `lkmut_highdose` to the low/mid-dose
value.

```{r fig5}
fig5_doses <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(3:8, 14:16), amt = 2500)
tv_fig5 <- rxode2::ini(tv, lkmut_highdose = log(7.4e-3))
sim5 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  tv_fig5,
  make_events(fig5_doses, one_animal("erlotinib", 100), seq(0, 40, by = 0.02))
))

sim5 |>
  select(time, tumor_vol, cycling_cells, resistant_cells) |>
  pivot_longer(-time) |>
  mutate(name = recode(name,
    tumor_vol = "Tumor volume", cycling_cells = "Sensitive cells",
    resistant_cells = "Resistant cells"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Eigenmann 2017."
  )

# Digitised from Figure 5 at day 40: total 1270, resistant 650, sensitive 620 mm^3.
fig5_check <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("tumor_vol", "resistant_cells", "cycling_cells"),
  published = c(1270, 650, 620)
) |>
  mutate(simulated = sapply(quantity, function(q) value_at(sim5, 40, q)))
knitr::kable(fig5_check, digits = 0)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig5_check$simulated / fig5_check$published - 1) < 0.10))
```

# Figure 6: 20 daily doses of erlotinib 100 mg/kg

Figure 6 simulates 20 daily doses of 100 mg/kg from day 3 followed by a
27-day wash-out. Here the packaged high-dose parameters (k2 and kSR of the
100 mg/kg group) reproduce the figure.

```{r fig6}
fig6_doses <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 3:22, amt = 2500)
sim6 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  tv,
  make_events(fig6_doses, one_animal("erlotinib", 100), seq(0, 50, by = 0.02))
))

sim6 |>
  select(time, tumor_vol, cycling_cells, resistant_cells) |>
  pivot_longer(-time) |>
  mutate(name = recode(name,
    tumor_vol = "Tumor volume", cycling_cells = "Sensitive cells",
    resistant_cells = "Resistant cells"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(
    data = sim6, aes(time, frac_resistant * 1500), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1500, name = "Fraction of resistant cells (dashed)")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Eigenmann 2017."
  )

# Digitised from Figure 6 at day 50: total 1120, resistant 850, sensitive 280 mm^3;
# the resistant fraction is close to 1 from day 20 to day 35.
fig6_check <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("tumor_vol", "resistant_cells", "cycling_cells"),
  published = c(1120, 850, 280)
) |>
  mutate(simulated = sapply(quantity, function(q) value_at(sim6, 50, q)))
knitr::kable(fig6_check, digits = 0)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fig6_check$simulated / fig6_check$published - 1) < 0.10),
  value_at(sim6, 25, "frac_resistant") > 0.95
)
```

During treatment the sensitive cells are killed and the tumor shrinks, then
regrows from slowly growing resistant cells; once dosing stops, the surviving
sensitive cells regrow at their faster rate and the resistant fraction falls.

# Figures 3 and 4: visual predictive check of the study design

The study design of Supplementary Table S1 is simulated with between-animal
variability and residual error, 100 animals per arm, with the initial tumor
volume set to 107 mm^3 for every animal (the per-animal baseline volumes are
not published).

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20171031)
n_per_arm <- 100L
arms <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  drug = c("erlotinib", "gefitinib"),
  mgkg = c(6.25, 25, 100)
) |>
  mutate(arm = row_number())
covs_vpc <- arms |>
  slice(rep(seq_len(n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    TRT_GEFITINIB = as.integer(drug == "gefitinib"),
    DOSE_HIGH = as.integer(mgkg >= 100),
    COHDOSE = mgkg,
    TUM_VOL = 107
  )
dose_days <- function(drug, mgkg) {
  if (drug == "erlotinib" && mgkg >= 100) c(3:10, 14:16) else 3:16
}
doses_vpc <- covs_vpc |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(id = id, time = dose_days(drug, mgkg), amt = mgkg * 25)
ev_vpc <- make_events(
  doses_vpc,
  covs_vpc |> select(id, TRT_GEFITINIB, DOSE_HIGH, COHDOSE, TUM_VOL),
  seq(0, 30, by = 0.5)
)
sim_vpc <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_vpc, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  left_join(covs_vpc |> select(id, drug, mgkg), by = "id")

vpc_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  group_by(drug, mgkg, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.05), med = median(tumor_vol),
    hi = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(dose = factor(paste(mgkg, "mg/kg"), levels = c("100 mg/kg", "25 mg/kg", "6.25 mg/kg")))

ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(lo, 1), ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(y = med)) +
  facet_grid(drug ~ dose) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 1e4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)",
    caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval; compare the upper panels of Figures 3 and 4 of Eigenmann 2017."
  )
```

```{r vpc-check}
med_at <- function(drug_, mgkg_, t) {
  vpc_sum$med[vpc_sum$drug == drug_ & vpc_sum$mgkg == mgkg_ & vpc_sum$time == t]
}
vpc_tab <- tidyr::expand_grid(drug = c("erlotinib", "gefitinib"), mgkg = c(6.25, 25, 100)) |>
  mutate(
    day10 = mapply(med_at, drug, mgkg, 10),
    day30 = mapply(med_at, drug, mgkg, 30)
  )
vpc_tab |>
  mutate(mgkg = format(mgkg)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Drug" = drug, "Dose (mg/kg)" = mgkg, "Day 10" = day10, "Day 30" = day30) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Median simulated tumor volume (mm^3)")
# Figures 3 and 4: in the 100 mg/kg groups the median falls well below the
# starting volume by day 10, while the 6.25 and 25 mg/kg groups keep growing.
stopifnot(
  med_at("erlotinib", 100, 10) < 0.75 * 107,
  med_at("gefitinib", 100, 10) < 0.75 * 107,
  med_at("erlotinib", 6.25, 10) > 107,
  med_at("gefitinib", 6.25, 10) > 107
)
```

# Figure 7: continuous versus pulsed erlotinib in mice

Figure 7 compares 100 mg/kg daily with a pulsed schedule of 420 mg/kg every
5 days and 20 mg/kg on the other days (code S4: a 400 mg/kg pulse added to a
20 mg/kg daily dose), assuming resistant cells are killed while the plasma
concentration exceeds Cth. Both arms use the high-dose k2 and kSR, as in S4.
The packaged model switches the threshold kill off; here it is switched on
with `drugSlope_resistant = 9.21e-5` L/ug/day, the value of the S4 and S5
code. The paper's curves are means of 250 animals simulated with
between-animal variability, so the typical-value curves below are compared
with them qualitatively.

```{r fig7}
tv_kill <- rxode2::ini(tv, drugSlope_resistant = 9.21e-5)
cont_doses <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 3:102, amt = 100 * 25)
pulse_doses <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 3:102, amt = 20 * 25),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(3, 102, by = 5), amt = 400 * 25)
)
run_mouse <- function(model, doses, label) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    model,
    make_events(doses, one_animal("erlotinib", 100), seq(0, 100, by = 0.01))
  )) |>
    mutate(schedule = label)
}
sim7 <- bind_rows(
  run_mouse(tv_kill, cont_doses, "Continuous, 100 mg/kg daily"),
  run_mouse(tv_kill, pulse_doses, "Pulsed, 420 mg/kg + 4 x 20 mg/kg")
)

ggplot(sim7, aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = schedule)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical-value analogue of Figure 7b of Eigenmann 2017."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

auce7 <- sim7 |>
  group_by(schedule) |>
  summarise(
    Cmax = max(Cc),
    TVmin = min(tumor_vol),
    AUCE30 = auc_trap(time[time <= 30], tumor_vol[time <= 30]),
    AUCE100 = auc_trap(time, tumor_vol)
  )
knitr::kable(auce7, digits = 0)

# The typical animal's minimum tumor volume is far below the means of
# Table 3 (60.9 and 69.5 mm^3), which average 250 animals with
# between-animal variability; only the ordering of the schedules is compared.
# Without the threshold kill the two schedules give nearly the same tumor
# burden (Results: 'Similar PD responses were obtained ... (data not shown)').
sim7_nokill <- bind_rows(
  run_mouse(tv, cont_doses, "continuous"),
  run_mouse(tv, pulse_doses, "pulsed")
) |>
  group_by(schedule) |>
  summarise(AUCE100 = auc_trap(time, tumor_vol))
knitr::kable(sim7_nokill, digits = 0, caption = "AUCE to day 100 without the threshold kill")

stopifnot(
  # Figure 7a: continuous peaks are about twofold, pulsed peaks far above Cth.
  auce7$Cmax[1] > 7152, auce7$Cmax[2] > 4 * 7152,
  # Figure 7c and Table 3: lower tumor burden with the pulsed schedule.
  auce7$AUCE100[2] < auce7$AUCE100[1],
  abs(sim7_nokill$AUCE100[2] / sim7_nokill$AUCE100[1] - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Figure 8: hybrid model with human erlotinib PK

For the clinical scenarios (code S5) the mouse PK is replaced by human
erlotinib PK (Lu 2006: ka 22.8 1/day, V 233 L, ke 0.408 1/day; doses in ug)
while the tumor parameters stay at the mouse estimates. S5 uses kSR of the
high-dose group (0.00166 1/day) with the low/mid-dose erlotinib k2
(9.21e-5 L/ug/day) and the threshold kill of resistant cells. Three
schedules are compared from day 1: 150 mg daily for 28 days; 1050 mg on two
consecutive days each week with 50 mg on days 10-14, 17-21 and 24-28; and
1600 mg once a week with 50 mg on six days of weeks 2-4.

```{r fig8}
tv_human <- rxode2::ini(
  tv,
  lka = log(22.8), lkel = log(0.408), lvc = log(233),
  ldrugSlope_highdose = log(9.21e-5),
  drugSlope_resistant = 9.21e-5
)
human_animal <- one_animal("erlotinib", 100)
human_animal$COHDOSE <- 0
schedules8 <- list(
  "Continuous 150 mg" = data.frame(id = 1L, time = 1:28, amt = 150000),
  "Pulsed 2 x 1050 mg + 5 x 50 mg" = bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16, 22, 23), amt = 1050000),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(10:14, 17:21, 24:28), amt = 50000)
  ),
  "Pulsed 1 x 1600 mg + 6 x 50 mg" = bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(1, 8, 15, 22), amt = 1600000),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(10:15, 17:22, 24:29), amt = 50000)
  )
)
sim8 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(schedules8), function(nm) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    tv_human,
    make_events(schedules8[[nm]], human_animal, seq(0, 35, by = 0.01))
  )) |>
    mutate(schedule = nm)
}))

sim8 |>
  select(time, schedule, Cc, tumor_vol) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, tumor_vol)) |>
  mutate(name = recode(name, Cc = "Concentration (ug/L)", tumor_vol = "Tumor volume (mm^3)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = schedule)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, caption = "Replicates Figure 8 of Eigenmann 2017.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

fig8_check <- data.frame(
  schedule = names(schedules8),
  # Digitised from Figure 8: peak concentration (ug/L) and tumor volume at day 35 (mm^3).
  published_cmax = c(1800, 7700, 7300),
  published_tv35 = c(650, 515, 610)
) |>
  mutate(
    simulated_cmax = sapply(schedule, function(s) max(sim8$Cc[sim8$schedule == s])),
    simulated_tv35 = sapply(schedule, function(s) value_at(sim8[sim8$schedule == s, ], 35, "tumor_vol"))
  )
knitr::kable(fig8_check, digits = 0)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fig8_check$simulated_cmax / fig8_check$published_cmax - 1) < 0.10),
  all(abs(fig8_check$simulated_tv35 / fig8_check$published_tv35 - 1) < 0.10)
)
```

The simulated delay of regrowth under the pulsed schedules is small, as the
paper concludes: concentrations exceed the threshold only briefly.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Base TGI model not distributed.** Table 1 reports only the parameter
  count, residual error and AIC of the base model (Equations 4-8); its
  estimates are not published.
* **Joint model in one file.** The authors fitted both drugs simultaneously
  with shared tumor-growth, transit and conversion parameters, so the drug is
  selected with the `TRT_GEFITINIB` indicator rather than split into two
  files.
* **Initial tumor volume as a covariate.** Table 1 counts seven estimated
  parameters, all of which appear in Table 2, so TV0 was not estimated; it is
  the `TUM_VOL` covariate (the authors' code uses 107 mm^3).
* **Random effects are Monolix standard deviations.** Table 2 reports omega
  as a standard deviation, the Monolix convention; the `ini()` variances are
  their squares. The Results text quotes a range of 0.468-0.689, which does
  not match Table 2 (0.487-0.742); Table 2 is used. The S4 simulation code
  uses different values for lambda0 (0.543) and erlotinib k2 (0.437) and is
  not used for the variances.
* **High-dose random effects.** Table 2 gives no separate random effect for
  the high-dose kSR and erlotinib k2, so each group shares the random effect
  of its parameter. The S4 code uses equal variances for the two levels,
  which makes the two encodings equivalent in simulation.
* **Residual error.** Table 1 prints one residual error (0.136) for the
  combined error model; it is taken as the proportional component, and the
  unreported additive component is fixed to 0. The proportional PK residual
  error belongs to the earlier PK analysis and is not reported; it is fixed
  to 0.
* **PK parameters.** Table 2 lists the typical PK parameters and their
  random effects from the earlier report; in the PD fit the individual PK
  estimates were held fixed. ka is shared by both drugs and fixed (Table 2).
* **Threshold kill of resistant cells.** Equation 17 writes the kill term as
  `DER = k2R * Cp` above Cth and Equation 14 subtracts `DER` without
  multiplying by R; the S5 code uses `k2R * PK * R`, which is the form
  packaged. The S4 code (Figure 7) uses `k2R * (PK - Cth) * R` instead,
  so the Figure 7 analogue above differs slightly from the paper's
  simulation. The kill was not identifiable in the fit, so
  `drugSlope_resistant` is fixed to 0 in the packaged model.
* **Threshold value.** The text gives Cth as 7150 "ug/mL"; the units are
  ug/L (1 uM x 393.4 g/mol / 0.055 = 7153 ug/L), and the value 7152 of the
  S4 and S5 code is used. Figure 8 labels the threshold 7500 ug/L.
* **Parameter combinations of the simulation code.** Figure 5 (code S3)
  uses the high-dose k2 with the low/mid-dose kSR, and Figure 8 (code S5)
  the high-dose kSR with the low/mid-dose k2; the replications above set
  these combinations explicitly. Table 2 gives k1 = 1.52 and kSR (high dose)
  = 1.7e-3 1/day, while the code uses 1.51 and 0.00166; Table 2 is used.
  The S4 code also subtracts an extra `S_pulse * kSR_hd` term from the
  sensitive cells of the pulsed arm, and the S5 code feeds the third damaged
  compartment of the 1600 mg arm from the second compartment of the
  1050 mg arm; both look like typing errors and are not reproduced, which
  explains the small difference for the 1600 mg schedule in Figure 8.
* **Dose units.** Doses are in ug for a 25 g mouse (`C = 25` in the code),
  matching the PK peak of about 14,000 ug/L in Figure 5.
* **Units of the growth rates.** The code comments swap the units of
  lambda0 and lambda1; the units of Table 2 (1/day and mm^3/day) are used.
